page: Amazon Web Services t2.2xlarge is an x86_64 burstable general-purpose instance deployed on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The configuration allocates 8 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with a single thread per core, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and a shared 45 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, yielding a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 1 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and contains no local storage or discrete graphics hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate middle-tier aggregate throughput alongside constrained single-thread and memory write performance. Stress-ng returned scores of 1737.48 for single-core and 11556.72 for multi-core, both placing in the middle 50% band. PassMark recorded a CPU score of 10905.03, supported by solid database operation (5634.84) and extended instruction (8019.58) metrics. However, single-threaded processing reflects the older Broadwell architecture, shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 874.0, single-threaded gzip compression at 20.06 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression at 7.12 GB/sec, all in the lowest 10% percentile.

Data transmission and in-memory execution reflect significant architectural bottlenecks. While cached read memory bandwidth reaches 625.85 GB/sec, large uncached write operations drop to 24.83 GB/sec in the lower 25% percentile. Web serving throughput registered at 1.95 GB/sec, while Redis recorded 0.87 million SET operations per second. CPU-based machine learning inference rates remain constrained, managing 5.17 tokens per second on 7B parameter models for text generation and 70.69 tokens per second on 135M parameter models.

The t2.2xlarge instance trades continuous high compute throughput for cost-effective memory capacity and burstable capability. Because it relies on CPU credits, sustained heavy multi-core utilization will encounter throttling or burst surplus overhead. It is appropriately sized for variable enterprise workloads, intermediate staging environments, light build and CI/CD servers, and batch processing systems that experience irregular activity spikes rather than sustained, write-heavy database transactions.
description: Amazon Web Services t2.2xlarge is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine running on the Xen hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, it provides 8 vCPUs across 8 physical cores alongside 32.0 GB of RAM. The instance features a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps, with no local storage disks or dedicated GPUs included. Benchmark measurements indicate steady mid-range multi-core CPU throughput, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 10905.03 and multi-core Geekbench score of 4812.0. However, single-threaded tasks and uncached memory writes exhibit legacy hardware limitations, resulting in lower scores on decompression and Redis operations. The instance is suited for batch processing, dev/test environments, CI/CD pipelines, and intermittent application serving.
